meta.author: cps deep research
meta.description: CPS pension general-fund reserve split into the operating diversion and the State share; contingencies and vacancy factor explained from the budget book

splits.note: Budget-only reserve line (it is not a payment to anyone). Official explanation: the budget book says CPS pays $663.6M of the teacher pension fund's required $1,026.7M: $602.3M comes from the pension levy and $61.3M from the operating budget (p.36-37). The State pays the other $363.1M. The pieces below are our arithmetic from those published numbers (see each piece), not a CPS-published split of this line.

pieces.name: CPS operating money diverted to the teacher pension fund

source.doc: CPS FY2026 Budget Book, Pensions chapter (CPS' Employer Contribution Requirements)

pieces.why: The pension tax is not big enough to cover what CPS owes the teachers' pension fund, so CPS must add this much from its regular school money.
pieces.note: Method: Board required contribution $646,234,000 plus additional Board contribution $17,332,000 (CTPF valuation p.1) = $663,566,000, minus the $602,309,665 levy = $61,256,335. The budget book reports this gap as '$61.3 million' (operating revenue diversion).

pieces.name: State's share of the teacher pension that schools are not charged for

source.doc: CTPF Actuarial Valuation 6/30/2025, Executive Summary p.1

pieces.why: The State pays part of CPS teachers' pensions on CPS's behalf, and this part appears to be the matching cost in the budget (our reading of the numbers, not a CPS statement).
pieces.note: Method: remainder of the line. It matches the State's FY2026 share $363,094,000 (normal cost $346,838,000 + additional $16,256,000, CTPF valuation p.1) minus the $303,780,006 of teacher employer pension already charged to schools and programs (accounts A57105 + A57110), which is $59,313,994, within $11 of the remainder. Whole teacher pension chain ties: $1,160.594M (research/cps_deep.md section 1).

side.label: Budget book: contingencies are 'funding that has been budgeted but not yet allocated to specific accounts or units where it will eventually be spent'. 'Schools are not required to allocate all of their funds, but can hold some in contingency' and 'the District holds grant funds in contingency, particularly if the grant is not yet confirmed.' The contingency budget fell $155M from FY2025, driven largely by the end of pandemic-era grants.

splits.note: Official explanation: planned savings because some jobs will sit empty for part of the year (vacancy savings).

side.label: Budget book glossary: vacancy savings are 'the anticipated savings resulting from the delay in staffing new and vacant positions.' In the budget the vacancy factor is a single FY2026 program (Vacancy Factor, P109981) of -$200,000,000 in the General Education Fund: -$143,275,556 against teacher salaries and -$56,724,444 against career service salaries. It is a budget-only offset: CPS plans for salary lines to come in lower because it expects not to fill every job all year.
